Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argues that a part of the subject land measuring 1 acre was allotted to the petitioner by virtue of which, he became the owner; the land having been acquired without notifying his name, he had no opportunity of opposing the acquisition going by the scheme of section 28 of the 1966 Act; even otherwise, his client is entitled to compensation, should the challenge to acquisition be negatived.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner also points out in all fairness that some dispute as to Revenue entry in respect of the land is pending in revision before the jurisdictional Deputy Commissioner u/s 136(3) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964; once that is decided in his client's favour, the respondents are bound to pay the compensation for the land in question; he also adds that in several similar matters, this court has taken the same view.
He also seeks a direction for the expeditious disposal of the Revision.

sentences.text: After service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 & 2 are represented by the learned AGA; respondent No.3- SLAO of the KIADB is represented by the learned Senior Panel Counsel.
Petition against the 4th respondent is already dismissed on 3.9.2018.

Learned AGA and the Panel Counsel oppose the petition vehemently contending the scheme of acquisition envisaged u/s 28 of the 1966 Act, is bit in variance with that envisaged u/ss. 17 & 19 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 in the sense that acquisition notification is khata-specific unlike under the 1976 Act.

That being the position, the government was shown itself as khatedars in the Records and the acquisition proceedings have been accomplished decades ago, especially when petitioners' title is under cloud because of pendency of Revision Petition u/s 136(3) of the 1964 Act
, the Writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this court is inclined to grant indulgence in the matter as under and for the following reasons:
(a) The government notified acquisition of the entire Sy.No.40 in all admeasuring 206 Acres in which 1 Acre land in respect of which petitioner is laying the claim is subsumed.

Since the acquisition under 1966 Act is khata-specific as held by this court in a catena of decisions, the acquisition notifications cannot be faltered on the ground that it did not mention the name of petitioner when petitioner's name did not figure in the khata at all.

(b) The Preliminary Notification u/s 28(1) of the 1966 Act was issued on 4.11.2006;
petitioner not being the khatedar, obviously did not and could not file the objections and that cannot be helped at this length of time; the Final Notification u/s 28(4) was issued on 7.5.2007.
The question of Possession Delivery Notice u/s 28(6) would not arise since State itself was the khatedar and it after acquisition has transferred the subject land to the KIADB.
With this fact matrix, no much relief as sought for in the petition can be given to the petitioner.

(c) The above having been said, there is one more aspect which needs deliberation at the hands of this court, as rightly argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner; petitioner claims to be grantee of the subject land and it appears that some entries were made in his favour on the basis of the alleged grant; validity of the same is put in challenge before the Deputy Commissioner u/s 136(3) of the 1964 Act and the same is said to be still pending.

If the petitioner succeeds in the Revision Petition in the sense that the government looses it, he obviously can stake his claim for the payment of compensation by producing other evidentiary material to vouch the title.

In view of the above, this Writ Petition is disposed off with the following:
ORDER [i] The Deputy Commissioner, Bangalore Urban District, is directed to hear & dispose off the Revision Petition No.628/2008-09, in accordance with law and report compliance to the Registrar General of this Court, within an outer limit of three months reckoned from this day.

[iii] The petitioner shall be entitled to all the statutory benefits that would accrue by virtue of acquisition of the subject land under Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.
